title: LLMs and Childhood Safety: Identifying Risks and Proposing a Protection Framework for Safe Child-LLM Interaction

bias_targets.methodology: The paper proposes automated post-training testing of LLM outputs to evaluate language and connotations directed at specific genders, including checking for the reinforcement of professional stereotypes (e.g., linking 'doctor' to men and 'nurse' to women) and maintaining gender parity.

The framework suggests automated bias testing to identify and correct responses that link specific races with negative features, alongside an inclusiveness standard requiring at least 90% parity for ethnic diversity.

Recommends evaluating model outputs for job-related prejudices (such as biased associations with high-prestige occupations) and ensuring socioeconomic diversity parity to prevent skewed developmental perspectives in children.
